correctness.rationale: For a specified nonempty sink subset of one bipartition, forcing edges gives B_(a-r,b); sets intersecting both parts cannot be sinks. This proves the marked EGF exactly. H=1-(exp(x)-1)(exp(y)-1) has a strictly minimal smooth diagonal point at rho=log 2 by Khera–Lundberg Lemma 4.1, with Q=16*rho^3*(1-rho)>0. Entire numerators exp(zx+y) have compact-parameter uniformly bounded derivatives; ACSV Theorem 4.2 gives ratio exp((z-1)rho)+O_R(1/n), proving the limiting PGF, Cauchy geometric local errors and TV rate. The standalone checker verified finite exact distributions independently for all K_(a,b) with 1<=a,b<=4 and factorial moments plus numerical controls; no finite test is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The number of sinks is an intrinsic probabilistic statistic of the same dense acyclic orientations whose longest-path behavior is known to be Gaussian. Its full distribution instead converges to a nondegenerate zero-truncated Poisson(log 2) law, with uniform analytic O_R(1/n), total-variation O(1/n), and geometrically summable individual probability errors. This gives a quantitative finite-size benchmark and complete asymptotic multiplicity information, not just the known total counts, one-sink enumeration, or a routine parameter substitution.
